lead: A Python rename script must open with `newline=""` at both ends, or it rewrites every line of every file it touches.
body: `Path.read_text()`/`write_text()` default to universal newlines on the way in and `os.linesep` on the way out, so on Windows an LF file comes back CRLF and `git diff --numstat` reads the whole file as changed, burying the lines you meant. `git status` saying *"CRLF will be replaced by LF the next time Git touches it"* is the whole diagnosis; `tools/splice.py` gets this right, and a one-off script beside it does not inherit that.
